title: alchemilla alpina proles subsericea
intro: Alchemilla alpina proles subsericea, commonly known as the Alpine lady's mantle, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae. It is native to high-altitude mountainous regions, where it grows as a perennial herb with delicate, white flowers and serrated leaves. The plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may contribute to wound healing, antimicrobial activity, and improved digestion. The bioactive constituents of Alpine lady's mantle include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are believed to exhibit therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant effects.
